BrandingIn.description: `material: null` goes back to the built-in colours. `version` is what the admin saw.
BrandingIn.title: BrandingIn

BrandingOut.description:
The colours everyone sees. `material` is null for the built-in colours; `version` is 0
until an admin first saves.
BrandingOut.title: BrandingOut

MaterialTheme.description:
Brand colours from a Material Theme Builder export: the light and dark schemes (every
Material 3 role) and the five tonal palettes. app.domain.branding checks the exact keys.
MaterialTheme.title: MaterialTheme

post.description: Sets the password and signs the user in: they land on their dashboard (AFD J1).
Works with the cookie alone, so an expired access token can't stop a logout.

patch.description: Name, phone, time zone, theme and password. Viewers may edit their own profile.

post.description: Always 202: "If that email is registered, a link is on its way" (AFD J2).

Always the same answer for a new or an existing email, so registering can't be used
to find out who has an account.

get.description: Staff see every organization; a client sees only their own (rule 3).

patch.description: Deactivating blocks the organization's users from signing in; its data is kept (ORG-4).

post.description: Staff accounts are always created this way; clients can be invited too (AUTH-6).

patch.description:
Roles, organization, status, name and phone. Disabling logs the user out of every
device at once (AUTH-11).

post.description: Link a pending client to an existing organization or create one (AUTH-3, AFD J1 4).

Mint the link for a reset or invitation email at the moment it is sent. The token is
never in an event; minting again replaces it, so only the newest email's link works.
HTTP Basic with the service's name and secret (a Docker secret, TRD §6.4).

get.description: Current state for read-model backfill (TRD §8.6), shaped like the events' data.
